subject: research/radar-detection-twin
professional: a radar systems engineer (detection/CFAR specialist) who sizes sensors with Swerling target models, who would first check the CFAR loss against Richards/Skolnik, the K-clutter CFAR literature, and whether the texture correlation assumption matches the sea or ground clutter in question

evidence.correctness: Ran own script (scratchpad recompute.py, scipy/numpy, no import of the author's code) for: CA twin SNR 20.674 dB (matches 20.67; known-threshold Swerling-I 19.37 dB gives a 1.31 dB CFAR loss, textbook range), OS k=12 twin SNR 21.295 dB (21.30), real CA Pfa at nu=2 30.14x (30.1x) by my own nested quadrature, real OS k=12 35.1x by 20M-trial Monte Carlo (34.9x), real CA Pd 0.839 (0.839), repair 3.70 dB (3.70). One headline fails: the nu=2 SNR shortfall is 6.18 dB (own quad; 40M-trial MC Pd 0.90006 at my SNR) against the published 6.28/6.3, a 0.10 dB error from a grid clamp in TextureGrid.gfun; nu=5 and 20 are fine. 7 of 8 recomputed outputs pass; the one error is small and conclusions are unchanged.
evidence.completeness: Every claimed result is in results.txt, which the README command reproduces byte-for-byte (62 s). Exact laws, OS inflation table, repair cost, shortfall, ranking and shared-texture result all exist and run end to end. Figure present. Missing: LOG.md (optional), no K-distribution closed-form check which the paper itself lists as a limit.
evidence.verification: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 8 tests pass in 10.5 s. Six seeded mutations: the four logic changes (OS product range, OS beta exponent, simulator rank, CA law exponent/denominator) each failed 1-4 tests; shrinking slo caught; truncating the texture tail (yhi 6->2) survived. Tests cross-check closed forms against Monte Carlo, which is the right design, but tolerances are loose (4-8%), no test pins a results.txt number, and the one real numerical error (grid clamp, 0.1 dB) is untested.
evidence.craft: Read model.py (154 lines), tests, run.py. Small, readable, stdlib only, docstrings explain the maths, numerically careful (log-space order-statistic integral, midpoint rule). Defects: silent bracket returns in the bisections, a clamp in gfun that biases high-SNR Pd, a per-trial Python simulator. No dead code or copied engine beyond the stated repeat of radar-clutter-twin's quadrature (intentional, stated).
evidence.claims: Checked 5 claims. Pass: '~1% vs 400k simulation', stylised disclosure and limitations, rankings and shared-texture rows. Fail: '6.3 dB shortfall' (true about 6.2 dB, in README, paper and projects.json); 'exact law ... new here' is not hedged against the K-clutter CFAR literature, none of which is cited. The README also claims a reproduction time slightly above measured. Because one headline number and the novelty claim are not fully backed, claims is 2.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it: the code is clean, the laws verified by simulation, and the limitations are listed. But the qualitative result (CFAR is not robust to iid spiky clutter; OS and CA both lose; the threshold repair costs several dB) is known and the quantitative laws are textbook transforms; there is no real data, no sourced nu, and the realistic partial-correlation case is absent. Nearest prior work: Watts 1985, Armstrong & Griffiths 1991, Raghavan 1991, Gandhi & Kassam 1988, Conte et al. on CFAR in K clutter. Sound, not new enough for the PhD+ main-track bar in research/CLAUDE.md.
evidence.domain: Compared with radar-detection practice (Richards, Skolnik, Swerling-I with a CFAR loss; Albersheim/Neyman-Pearson reference points): the baseline numbers agree (CFAR loss 1.31 dB at N=16). Departures a radar engineer would flag: iid texture per cell is the pessimistic extreme (fully shared gives exact CFAR, paper item 6); the target is assumed to share the test cell's texture; no interferers or clutter edges, the case OS-CFAR exists for; single pulse, no pulse integration; nu chosen not sourced. A signed-off method for sizing a sensor would need the correlated-texture middle case.

defects.what: Headline SNR shortfall at nu=2 is 0.10 dB too high (6.28 stated as 6.3; true 6.18, 26.86 dB not 26.96). TextureGrid.gfun clamps to g[0] for s below e^-6, but at 27 dB SNR the arguments alpha/(N(1+s)tau) fall below that, and Pd^16 amplifies the error to 0.2% in Pd. Own quadrature and a 40M-trial Monte Carlo agree with each other and with a finer grid, not with results.txt. Does not change any conclusion; the propagated figures are in README, paper, projects.json and results.txt.

No test pins grid accuracy at the operating point of the headline (nu=2, Pfa 1e-4, Pd 0.9 at 27 dB). The tests only compare Pfa at 1e-2 or Pd at SNR 6 to 200k-trial Monte Carlo with 4-8% tolerances (about 6-11 sigma), so a quadrature error of 0.2% in Pd, or an OS-law error of a few percent, passes; truncating the texture tail (yhi 6->2) also survives. No test asserts any number in results.txt.

Prior work is not cited and novelty is overstated: CA/OS/CMLD-CFAR in K-distributed clutter with iid texture, including false-alarm inflation and detection loss, is a standard topic (Watts 1985; Armstrong & Griffiths 1991; Raghavan 1991; Gandhi & Kassam 1988; Conte, Longo, Lops and Gini, Farina, Greco on CFAR in compound-Gaussian clutter). Only Finn-Johnson, Rohling and Ward are cited. 'New' OS law is the textbook Beta transform of the marginal cdf. No comparison to published K-clutter CFAR loss curves was made, which would have been the independent check of the quadrature.

The central inflation result depends on iid texture per reference cell, which the paper's own item 6 shows disappears under fully shared texture; real sea clutter texture is correlated over a range of cells and pulses. The intermediate (partial correlation) case, the one a radar engineer would want, is not modelled, and the ranking result is by construction because interferers and outliers are excluded. The paper discloses both but frames the 6.3 dB as 'what a twin should promise'.

'Stylised' label with no sourced parameters: nu values 1.5, 2, 5, 20 and N=16 are chosen, not taken from measured sea-clutter shape-parameter ranges (e.g. Ward, Tough, Watts 2006 give nu from below 1 to above 20 by grazing angle and resolution) or a datasheet; the brief asks that a headline parameter be sourced.

alpha_for_pfa and snr_for_pd bisect on fixed brackets (hi=1e6, 1e9) and silently return the bracket end when the target is unreachable instead of raising; simulate() runs trial loops in pure Python (about 10 s of the 10.5 s test time).
No LOG.md and no project.json, so the project card lives in the shared projects.json; the README test-runtime and experiment-runtime figures (15 s, 70 s) are a little high (10.5 s, 62 s measured).

verdict: Sound, cleanly built and fully reproducible (tests pass, results.txt regenerates byte-identically, seven of eight independent recomputations agree to MC precision, including the 30x and 35x inflation figures and the 20.67 dB promise). One headline number, the nu=2 SNR shortfall, is 0.10 dB too high (6.28 vs 6.18) from a quadrature clamp that no test pins. The project does not meet the bar because the novelty of the 'new' OS-CFAR law is not placed against the K-clutter CFAR literature, which it does not cite, and the iid-texture assumption that drives the result is the pessimistic extreme with the realistic partially correlated case missing. It is finished, a decent replication-grade study, below the PhD+ research bar.
